plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree covered in clouds of pale pink-white, five-petaled blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is widely planted in parks, along rivers, and in gardens across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in much of the Northern Hemisphere (peak varies by latitude)
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is the main tree celebrated during Japan's hanami festivals, and the 1912 gift of 3,000 trees from Tokyo to Washington D.C. established the famed National Cherry Blossom Festival.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with a pale yellow outer perianth and a deeper yellow trumpet-shaped corona. It grows in meadows, open woodlands, and gardens, and naturalizes readily.
plants.location: Western Europe (UK, France, Spain, Belgium); widely cultivated and naturalized in North America and elsewhere
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, making it toxic to most animals, and galantamine, a compound derived from related Amaryllidaceae plants, is used in medicine to treat Alzheimer's symptoms.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree with large, goblet-shaped flowers that open on bare branches in early spring. The tulip-like blossoms are often white inside and flushed pink to purple on the outside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to April in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated across the UK, the eastern and western United States, and Europe; hybrid originated in France
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, evolving before bees existed, and their sturdy flowers are thought to have evolved to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped flowers in late summer to autumn of the Southern Hemisphere. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering and die back in summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the Southern Hemisphere (autumn)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, Chile, and California
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed 'Naked Lady' because the flower stalks emerge on bare ground with no leaves, appearing suddenly after autumn rains or the end of summer heat.
